question: Small-scale coastal fishing is a key pillar for many island and coastal communities in Greece. The Commission itself published a specific guide (vademecum) on the allocation of fishing opportunities in November 2025, recognising that small-scale fishers are particularly vulnerable and that Member States must apply transparent and objective social, economic and environmental criteria.

On 24 March 2026, in view of the Agriculture and Fisheries Council of 30 March, the Commission returned to the issue, pointing out that small-scale coastal fishing accounts for 76 % of the EU fleet, while 23 % of vessels are already operating at a loss.

Nevertheless, in areas of the Mediterranean, fishers have dropped below 130 fishing days, with income losses of up to 40-50 %, which is particularly harmful to the Greek islands. In view of the above: 1.

Does the Commission intend to ask Member States to give special priority to smallscale coastal and island fisheries when implementing Article 17 of the Regulation on the Common Fisheries Policy and the allocation of fishing opportunities and fishing days?

Does the Commission intend to activate targeted financial support through the EMFAF for fishers in island and coastal areas who are disproportionately affected by the restrictions in the Mediterranean?

Will the Commission review the current system of fishing limitations in the Mediterranean on the basis of updated scientific and socio-economic data by maritime zone, in order to avoid horizontal measures that lead to the economic suffocation of the primary sector on the islands?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (8.6.2026) Through the Communication for enhanced transparency and good governance in the allocation of fishing opportunities by Member States1, published in November 2025, the Commission encouraged Member States to use the full potential of Article 17 of the Common Fisheries Policy Regulation (CFP) Regulation2 to support small-scale and coastal fishers.

Nevertheless, the Commission recognised that it is Member States’ responsibility to decide on their national allocation systems and that it has no legal tool to oblige Member States to allocate fishing opportunities to small-scale coastal and island fisheries.

The Greek European Maritime, Fisheries and Aquaculture Fund (EMFAF) programme provides key support for the resilience and competitiveness of the fisheries sector and coastal communities. This includes a wide range of activities, such as diversifying activities to support income, like fishing tourism, mitigating impacts from climate change, enhancing fishers' skills and income possibilities through training.

Moreover, projects related to smallscale fisheries may be supported at an aid intensity of up to 100%. The conservation of marine biological resources and the management of fisheries are based on the best available scientific advice and on a consultation process with advisory bodies and Member States, both fundamental principles of the CFP.

The specificities and the technical characteristics of the type of fisheries are being considered in this regard. Furthermore, at regional level within the General Fisheries Commission for the Mediterranean, a subregional approach is followed to ensure proportionate and tailor-made measures.
1 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=OJ:C_202506227. 2 Regulation (EU) No 1380/2013 of the European Parliament and of the Council

of 11 December 2013 on the Common Fisheries Policy, amending Council Regulations (EC) No 1954/2003 and (EC) No 1224/2009 and repealing Council Regulations (EC) No 2371/2002 and (EC) No 639/2004 and Council Decision 2004/585/EC.
